kinds.a: single-family detached home · free-standing house · stand-alone house
kinds.d: A free-standing house sharing no walls with neighbours, on its own plot.
A house sharing one party wall with its neighbour, usually built as a mirror-image pair.

kinds.a: terrace · row house · row home · brownstone (US) · back-to-back
kinds.d: A house in a continuous row sharing side walls with neighbours on both sides.
A multi-storey urban house on a small footprint, usually terraced or close-set; historically a grandee's city residence.
A single-storey house, whether detached, semi-detached or terraced, sometimes with rooms set in the roof.
t: Dormer or chalet bungalow (rooms in roof)

kinds.d: A small, modest house, typically in a rural or semi-rural setting.
The principal dwelling of a farm, sold with or without its land and outbuildings; see Farm in Land & estates.

kinds.a: mews property · coach house · carriage house conversion
kinds.d: A house in a mews: a converted stable or carriage house with living quarters behind large city houses.

kinds.a: ranch-style house · rambler · rancher · California ranch
kinds.d: A single-storey American house with a long, low profile and open plan; distinct from a working ranch.
A comfortable detached house with garden, usually in Mediterranean, resort or suburban use.
